text:
release-lead: Quick sync — rolling out a small but important change to our deploy orchestration policy and running a mandatory rollback drill next Tue 09:30 PT. Read fast: this affects canary gating, risk signals, and oncall responsibilities.

maria: Do we need a freeze for the drill or can normal deploys continue? :thinking_face:

release-lead: No full freeze. We will have a temporary canary-only window for the drill (09:30-10:00 PT). Production traffic continues; only new release canaries will be targeted by the drill.

alex: Who's running the drill? I can be primary if SRE needs a hand.

release-lead: Primary: eng-sre oncall (@oncall). Backup: alex. Ops owner: jordan. Please block the slot.

jordan: Can you paste the exact risk thresholds so I can update the runbook?

release-lead: Sure. New risk-signal thresholds (effective immediately):
- abort canary if error-rate (client 5xx) > 0.5% for 5m window
- abort if request p95 latency > 800ms for 5m window
- abort if model output regression score increases > 3% on our smoke prompts

Also added an automated mitigation path: if abort triggers, system will:
1) scale down canary to 0 traffic
2) switch routing to fallback model variant
3) create a rollback run in the deploy dashboard and notify #eng-oncall and the release channel

alex: Nice. How do we invoke a manual rollback from CLI?

release-lead: Command we added to rdeploy-tool:```
rdeploy rollback --deploy-id DEPLOY_ID --reason "rollback-drill"
```
Add `--no-confirm` only if you're oncall. The internal deploy-bot will post a confirmation message including links to the failure traces.

sam: Will this touch Dedicated pools? We have an enterprise customer on a long-running pool.

release-lead: It can. We set a policy: for Dedicated pools with pinned capacity, the abort path prefers model variant fallback rather than immediate teardown. We won't force-terminate pinned jobs unless you run `--force` with justification.

maria: Please add a short checklist to the Release Playbook and the weekly release mail. Link? https://internal.docs/release-playbook#rollback-drills

release-lead: Done — updated page and added the checklist. Also created a short runbook snippet for the oncall:```
- verify deploy-id in dashboard
- run logs: rlogs follow --deploy-id DEPLOY_ID
- if automated rollback failed: escalate to eng-sre pager and run `rdeploy rollback --deploy-id DEPLOY_ID --force`
```

devops-bot: Reminder: Drill scheduled Tue 09:30 PT. Automated alerts will be sent to #eng-oncall and the release-runner webhook.

jordan: One last ask: add a fake failure scenario to the canary sim so the drill is deterministic. I can PR a test.

release-lead: Please do. Create PR against infra-deploy/sim-canary-tests and tag @release-lead. We'll run the sim 30m before the drill.

alex: ACK, adding PR now. :thumbsup:

maria: Thx all. post-mortem template for the drill? small one, just list timing/owner/actions.

release-lead: Yep — use the new lightweight template at https://internal.docs/templates/rollback-drill. I'll take the first post-mortem.

sam: Heads up — I'll be unavailable during drill window but backup is alex.

release-lead: Noted. Backup list: alex -> jordan -> release-lead.

alex: ping if you want me to trigger rollback during drill otherwise I'll observe.

release-lead: Prefer observation first; we'll only flip to manual if automated path doesn't cleanly abort within 2 mins.

maria: All clear from PM side. Will include a short customer-facing note if we exercise rollback on production traffic.

devops-bot: Drill complete: simulation passed locally. Will post final status after Tue run.

jordan: Thanks — I'll prep the sim PR and the runbook update.

release-lead: Great. If anyone spots build or infra blockers before Tue, flag here. Otherwise see you at 09:15 PT for alignment. :rocket:
